headline: High-risk shared-workspace and output-chaining between Chatwoot and Flowise can leak customer data and amplify unsafe actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can ingest external messages and reports, while Flowise can read/write server files and run browser/tool nodes. A shared filesystem or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content from Chatwoot be treated as instructions by Flowise. The pathway is plausible but not proven by docs alone.
conditions: IF Chatwoot content is exported into a Flowise-readable file or prompt
IF Flowise flow nodes parse Chatwoot text as instructions without sanitization
mitigations: Separate the two systems onto different workspaces
Strip instructions from imported Chatwoot text
Add a prompt-injection filter before Flowise ingestion
Use read-only exports for any Chatwoot-to-Flowise transfer

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages; Flowise reads uploaded files and server filesystem and sends data to model providers or HTTP tools. If Chatwoot artifacts are placed in Flowise's workspace, sensitive customer data can be exfiltrated to third parties by default. The pairwise leakage path is credible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF customer records or conversation exports from Chatwoot are stored in Flowise's server filesystem
IF a Flowise flow sends those files to model providers or HTTP tools
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot exports out of Flowise storage
Disable file-based ingestion for sensitive conversations
Restrict Flowise tool nodes to approved endpoints
Redact customer identifiers before any transfer
requires-engineering: enforce per-workspace access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress and Flowise has broad network egress plus write_filesystem and shared_state_with_other_instances via server datastore. Even without git or shell writes, both can mutate shared operational state or external services, creating overlapping write surfaces and race-prone conflicts in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared workspace or datastore
IF Flowise flows update artifacts that Chatwoot also consumes or overwrites
mitigations: Assign separate directories and databases
Disable concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Serialize updates through one orchestrator
Use per-run namespaces for Flowise outputs
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot produces customer-facing messages and reports, and Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder that can act on tool outputs. If Flowise consumes Chatwoot output as authoritative, it can propagate hallucinations or malformed support content into downstream actions or responses. The default risk is strong because no verification mechanism is shown.
conditions: IF Flowise uses Chatwoot-generated text as a tool input or decision source
IF no human or automated verification step checks Chatwoot outputs before action
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action-taking node
Require human approval for customer-impacting actions
Constrain Flowise to read-only summarization of Chatwoot output
Log provenance for every Chatwoot-derived field
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly handles customer data and interaction history, while Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and can route them to model providers or HTTP tools. If regulated customer data is moved from Chatwoot into Flowise, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the higher justified severity.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from Chatwoot is processed inside Flowise flows
IF Flowise retention or provider logging differs from Chatwoot policy
mitigations: Classify data before routing into Flowise
Block regulated records from noncompliant flows
Align retention settings across both systems
Document provider logging for Flowise tool calls
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
